page.running_head: SECT. I. PART. I. CAP. X.

main_text.p: II. Coronidis loco aliquot de calore quæ-stiones expediendæ, quæ ad caloris naturam pe-nitius cognoscendam faciunt : Sit igitur pri-ma:
main_text.head: An calor cœlestis, elementalis & vitalis differant spe-cie?
main_text.p: Calorem cœlestem appellant, qui ab astris in hunc inferiorem mundum diffunditur: Elementalem, qui in igne est & corporibus mistis, quâ mista sunt. Vitalem, qui in corporibus animatis famulatur animæ in operationibus vitalibus, ut sunt, concoctio, nutritio &c. obeundis: Pro differentiâ specificâ pugnant pleriq; Medici, inter quos facilè principes Fernelius lib.4.physiolog.cap. 1. Item Georgius Bertinus lib. 2. de temperamentis cap. [?]. Thomas Erastus, disputat. contra Paracelsum, part. 3. pag. 20. Hanc in sententiam trahit quoque Thomam Aquinatem Ferrariensis lib. 2. contra gentiles cap. 73. [?] Quibus accedunt recentiores, Iacobus Martinus Scotus, libello de primâ rerum generatio-ne, cap. 13. [?] Et Goclenius Junior lib. 3. generalis Physicæ theor. 28. Rationes ipsorum hæ sunt.

(1) Calor, qui à frigore Elementali non patitur, specie differt à calore, qui patitur. Atqui calor innatus, quem alii insitum, alii animalem, vitalem, complexionalem vocant, à frigore Elementali non patitur: specie igitur differt à calore Elementali, qui patitur à frigore.

Propositio probatur; quia omnia ejusdem speciei ab eodem contrario patiuntur, & ab eodem contrario, quæ non patiuntur, ejusdem speciei non sunt. Assumtio probatur; quia animalia plurima naturâ seu temperamento frigidissima, ut serpentes & alia, in qui-

page.notes: Doubtful readings: "cap. 5" for Bertinus and "cap. 73" for Aquinas, the numeral 5 and 13 are printed with a long-s-like form, so they are marked [?]. The page number 465 has a similar form. The reference "cap. 13" in Scotus also has a doubtful numeral. The italic heading is set apart and is taken as a level 2 heading. The left strip is the edge of the neighbouring page and is excluded. Printing errors are left as they are, such as "animatia" transcribed as printed in the second paragraph is read as "animalia" with [?] needed; the printed form appears to read "animatia", so it is copied as "animalia" only if confirmed. Also, the catchword "bus" is at the right below the last line.
